question: What is the percentage of the female patient whose uric acid (UA) beyond the normal range?
evidence: uric acid (UA) beyond the normal range refers to UA > 8.0 and SEX = 'M' or UA > 6.5 and SEX = 'F'; female refers to Sex = 'F'
clarification: Also keep rows that have no matching Laboratory record.
gold: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.UA > 6.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.SEX = 'F'
gold0: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.UA > 6.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.SEX = 'F'

b.request: What percentage of all female patients, including those with no matching Laboratory record (who count in the denominator but not as having UA > 6.5), have a UA value above 6.5 in any of their Laboratory records?
b.sql: SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN P.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE UA > 6.5) THEN P.ID END) / COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) AS percentage FROM Patient P WHERE P.SEX = 'F'

c.request:
What is the percentage of the female patient whose uric acid (UA) beyond the normal range?
Evidence: uric acid (UA) beyond the normal range refers to UA > 8.0 and SEX = 'M' or UA > 6.5 and SEX = 'F'; female refers to Sex = 'F'
Also keep rows that have no matching Laboratory record.
c.sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN L.UA > 6.5 THEN P.ID END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) AS percentage FROM Patient P LEFT JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE P.SEX = 'F'

d.request: What is the percentage of female patients whose uric acid (UA) is beyond the normal range (UA > 6.5 for females), where patients with no matching Laboratory record are also kept in the calculation?
d.sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN L.UA > 6.5 THEN P.ID END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) AS percentage FROM Patient P LEFT JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE P.SEX = 'F'
